statBlock.specialAbilities:
SRD type: Hag

Although different hags are unique in appearance and mannerism, they have many aspects in common. All take the form of crones whose bent shapes belie their fierce power and swiftness.

Hags speak Giant and Common.

Combat

Hags are tremendously strong. They are naturally resistant to spells and can cast magic of their own. Hags often gather to form coveys. A covey, usually containing one hag of each type, can use powers beyond those of the individual members.

Special Attacks: Improved grab, rake 1d6+7, rend 2d6+10, spell-like abilities

Special Qualities: Damage reduction 2/bludgeoning, darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 19

Imported from the d20 SRD; verify attacks and skills in-game. Full rules at d20srd.org.
statBlock.organization: Solitary or covey (3 hags of any kind plus 1-8 ogres and 1-4 evil giants)

system.biography:
An annis commonly uses its disguise self ability to take the form of an exceptionally tall human, a fair giant, or an ogre.

An annis stands some 8 feet tall and weighs about 325 pounds.

Combat

Though physically powerful, these hags do not favor simple assaults but try to divide and confuse their foes before combat. They love to pose as commoners or gentlefolk to lull their victims into a sense of false security before they attack.

Improved Grab (Ex)

To use this ability, an annis must hit a Large or smaller opponent with a claw attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.

Rake (Ex)

Attack bonus +13 melee, damage 1d6+7. An annis can attack a grappled foe with both claws at no penalty.

Rend (Ex)

An annis that hits with both claw attacks latches onto the opponent’s body and tears the flesh. This attack automatically deals an extra 2d6+10 points of damage.

Spell-Like Abilities

3/day—disguise self, fog cloud. Caster level 8th.

system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Listen checks and Spot checks.

system.description: You are skilled at fighting opponents you cannot clearly see.
system.benefit:
In melee, every time you miss because of concealment, you can reroll your miss chance percentile roll one time to see if you actually hit.

An invisible attacker gets no advantages related to hitting you in melee. That is, you don't lose your Dexterity bonus to Armor Class, and the attacker doesn't get the usual +2 bonus to hit you. The invisible attacker's bonuses do still apply for ranged attacks, however.

You take only half the usual penalty to speed for being unable to see. Darkness and poor visibility in general reduces your speed to three-quarters normal, instead of one-half.
system.special: A fighter may select Blind-Fight as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You have a knack for avoiding death.
system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Fortitude saving throws.

system.description: You know how to tell a lie.
You can use this skill to persuade others to agree with your arguments, to resolve differences, and to gather valuable information or rumors from people.
You are skilled at changing your appearance.
Make a Hide check to conceal yourself from enemies, slink past guards, slip away without being noticed, or sneak up on people without being seen or heard.
You can use this skill to frighten opponents or to get them to act in a way that benefits you.
Your Listen check is either made against a DC that reflects how quiet the noise is that you might hear, or it is opposed by the target's Move Silently check.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.

What it does (SRD): If the creature hits with a listed natural weapon, it can attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. Details (size modifiers, opposed checks, holding vs pinning) follow the grapple rules.

ThirdEra: This template has no numeric rows in Mechanical effects or Capability grants. Track grapple state in play; use the NPC’s natural attacks and CMB/CMD from the sheet when resolving the grapple.

What it does (SRD): When the creature grapples or sometimes when it pounces, it can make extra natural attacks (usually two claw rakes) at the listed attack bonus against a grappled or appropriate target.

ThirdEra: Add rake attacks to the NPC’s Natural attacks list on the sheet (or note them in Description) so attack bonuses match the stat block. This template keeps Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty.

What it does (SRD): If the creature hits the same foe with two or more specified natural weapons in the same round, it deals extra damage (often the same dice as one claw plus a static bonus—use the stat block’s exact amount).

ThirdEra: Leave Mechanical effects empty unless you mirror a specific printed bonus. Rend damage is normally read straight from the monster entry after you confirm both attacks hit.
Spell-Like Abilities: Annis hag SLAs per SRD (typically including disguise self, fog cloud, hold person, polymorph, weakness, at caster level as listed in its statistics).
